## Appearance

Rosemary West is a tall, fair, and placid woman with a finely shaped face and a high white forehead. She has large, tranquil, heavenly blue eyes that convey a slow, sweet smile, and her warm, golden hair—resembling the color of new molasses taffy—is worn pinned in sleek, close coils around her head.

## Personality

Rosemary West is a sweet, delightful, and charming girl who makes a strong positive impression on those around her. She is a fine housekeeper and possesses skill as a music teacher, an endeavor she pursues out of personal enjoyment rather than necessity.

## History

Rosemary West grew up in the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), where her little brother died, she kept a pet hen, and she attended school with local boys. After her mother's death, she stayed closely at home with her sister [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md), with whom she clasped hands over their mother's Bible to vow they would never marry and would always live together. Years later, Rosemary met the widowed minister [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) by a hidden spring in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley). Though [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) warned her against romance, John visited their home, and Rosemary later comforted his daughter [Faith](../character/faith.md), earning the family's deep affection. When John eventually proposed, Rosemary realized she loved him and asked for time to consider, but [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) strictly refused to release her from her vow, forcing Rosemary to send John a cold rejection letter. Later, [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) approached Rosemary at the spring to ask her to release [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) from her vow so they could marry, which Rosemary granted; however, [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) then refused to marry Norman if Rosemary was left living alone. Deeply moved when John's young daughter [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) selflessly visited her and begged her to marry her father, Rosemary comforted the child, agreed to the proposal, and wrote a letter asking John to meet her.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P0](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P2](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0002), [v5 CHAPTER II. ## Quotes

> "It is such a help to talk things over. I know. I don’t suppose I can be as good at understanding as Mrs. Blythe—but I promise you that I won’t laugh."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P14](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0014)

> "But I would have been just as naughty, Faith—I wouldn’t have told him they were scorching—and I don’t believe I would ever have been a bit sorry for my wickedness, either."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P28](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0028)

> "Dearest, if a minister doesn’t behave as a gentleman we are not bound to respect his coat-tails. I know I would just have loved to see Jimmy Perry’s coat-tails burning up. It must have been fun."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P30](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0030)

> "If you hang the cage far enough from the wall I don’t think the cat could harm it. I’ll tell you just how to take care of it and I’ll bring it to Ingleside for you the next time I come down."
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P35](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0035)

> “Una, dear,” she said softly. “It isn’t because of you poor little souls that I cannot be your father’s wife. I never thought of such a thing. You are not bad—I never supposed you were. There—there was another reason altogether, Una.”
>
> — Rosemary West — [v5 CHAPTER XXXIV. UNA VISITS THE HILL P17](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0017)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--rosemary-west.md)

Rosemary forms a warm bond with [Anne](../character/anne.md), who considers her a delightful friend and part of the imaginative "race of [Joseph](../character/joseph.md)." Their friendship develops amidst shared community connections, and Rosemary helps care for the town's children, including soothing the Meredith children alongside Ingleside's household after a ghost scare in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley).

- Friend of — delightful friend whom she considers part of the race of Joseph  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XVII. A DOUBLE VICTORY P78](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0078)</sub>

### [Ellen West](../character/ellen-west.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--rosemary-west.md)

Rosemary and her sister [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) live together at the [West](../character/west.md) homestead, sharing a close bond that is strained by a past commitment. Ten years prior, the sisters made a solemn vow over their mother's Bible never to marry. When [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) begins courting Rosemary, [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) strictly holds her sister to the promise, creating deep sorrow and tension between them despite their mutual affection.

- Sibling of — sister  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), +9 more</sub>

### [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/john-meredith--rosemary-west.md)

After meeting at a hidden spring in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) falls deeply in love with Rosemary, viewing her as the only woman for him. Though Rosemary reciprocates his love, she initially sends him a heartbroken refusal due to a secret vow made to her sister. Their romantic path remains fraught until the children intervene, leading Rosemary to send word agreeing to meet him.

- Romantically involved with — he asked her to marry him and considers her the only woman in the world for him  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXI. ### [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/norman-douglas--rosemary-west.md)

[Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) is described as an intended brother-in-law to Rosemary through his desire to marry her sister, [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md). When Norman confronts Rosemary in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) to release [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) from her childhood vow, Rosemary readily consents, though complications between the sisters initially leave his marriage prospects with [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) uncertain.

- presumed Sibling of — intended brother-in-law by marriage to her sister  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXXII. TWO STUBBORN PEOPLE P1](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0001)</sub>

### [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/rosemary-west--una-meredith.md)

Rosemary acts as a gentle, comforting figure to young [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) and her siblings. Driven by a selfless wish to see her father happy, [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) visits the [West](../character/west.md) homestead to beg Rosemary to marry Mr. Meredith, prompting a deeply reassuring response from Rosemary and opening the door to the family's reconciliation.

- Friend of — friend and helper  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXXIV. UNA VISITS THE HILL P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)</sub>
